chapter_name: Early Humans and Beginning of Civilisation
learning_objective: 🎯 Trace the incredible journey of humanity from nomadic hunter-gatherers to settled farmers, leading to the birth of the first great civilisations!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Early humans lived as nomads in the Paleolithic Age. They used crude stone tools, hunted animals, gathered fruits, and discovered how to control fire.
A massive turning point where humans learned to grow crops (agriculture) and domesticate animals. This meant they no longer had to wander; they could settle in one place.
One of the greatest inventions of the Neolithic Age. The wheel revolutionized transport and made pottery making much easier and faster.

As farming produced surplus food, villages grew into cities. People specialized in jobs (weavers, traders). This led to the rise of Civilisations along river valleys (like the Indus Valley, Egypt, and Mesopotamia).
India's earliest civilisation on the banks of the river Indus. It was famous for its brilliant urban planning, grid-system streets, baked brick houses, and excellent drainage systems.

fun_activity.title: 🔥 Stone Age Inventor
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you are an early human who just discovered fire. Make a list of 3 ways fire will instantly change your life tonight! (E.g., scaring wild animals, cooking meat, staying warm).

exam_tips: 📌 The 'Neolithic Revolution' refers specifically to the transition from hunting-gathering to agriculture. Understand why this is called a 'revolution'.
📌 Why did early civilisations grow near rivers? (Answer: Fertile soil for farming, water for drinking/irrigation, and transportation).
📌 Be able to list at least 3 key features of the Indus Valley Civilisation's town planning (Drainage, Great Bath, Grid streets).
quick_recap: ⭐ The discovery of fire provided warmth, light, and protection from predators.
⭐ Settled agriculture allowed humans to build permanent homes and accumulate surplus food.
⭐ The Bronze Age followed the Stone Age, as humans learned to mix copper and tin.
